nameStory: The Darkface Arion gets its name from the distinctive dark coloring around its face and tentacles, which helps distinguish it from other slugs in the Arion genus. The scientific name 'distinctus' literally means 'distinguished' or 'distinct,' referring to these clear identifying features that set it apart from its slug relatives.
description: The Darkface Arion is a medium-sized land slug that belongs to the roundback slug family, named for their characteristic rounded, dome-like shape when at rest. Like all slugs, it's essentially a snail without a shell, breathing air through a lung-like organ. These terrestrial mollusks are soft-bodied creatures that glide along on a muscular foot, leaving behind a telltale slime trail. They typically reach about 2-3 inches in length when fully extended.

idTips.label: Dark face markings
idTips.description: Look for noticeably darker coloration around the head area and eye tentacles, creating a distinctive 'masked' appearance that contrasts with the body color

idTips.label: Rounded body shape
idTips.description: When disturbed or resting, the slug contracts into a characteristic dome or hump shape rather than flattening out completely

idTips.label: Slime trail texture
idTips.description: Leaves behind a clear, sticky mucus trail that feels slippery between your fingers and may have an iridescent sheen in sunlight

idTips.label: Breathing pore location
idTips.description: The pneumostome (breathing hole) is located on the right side of the body, appearing as a small opening that may open and close rhythmically

idTips.label: Body color variation
idTips.description: Overall body color ranges from brown to grayish, often with a mottled or speckled pattern, but the dark facial markings remain consistent

habitat: Darkface Arions prefer moist, shaded environments typical of New England's deciduous and mixed forests, particularly areas with rich, organic soil and plenty of leaf litter. You'll often find them under logs, rocks, or in compost piles where they can stay cool and humid. They also frequent garden areas with loose, well-composted soil, especially after rain or in the early morning when dew provides extra moisture.

seasonality.spring: Most active as temperatures warm and spring rains provide ideal humid conditions. Look for them emerging from winter hiding spots under logs and leaf litter.
seasonality.summer: Active during cooler, humid periods, especially after rain showers. During hot, dry spells they retreat to moist hiding places and become less visible.
seasonality.fall: Very active as they feed heavily before winter, often seen on damp autumn evenings. This is an excellent time for observation as they prepare for dormancy.
seasonality.winter: Largely inactive, hiding deep under logs, rocks, or in soil crevices. Rarely seen unless you disturb their winter shelters on milder days.

funFact: Slugs like the Darkface Arion can have up to 27,000 tiny teeth arranged on a rasping tongue called a radula, which they use like a living cheese grater to scrape food into digestible bits!
confusionNotes: The Darkface Arion can be confused with other Arion slugs, but remember the 'masked bandit' trick - if the face and tentacles are noticeably darker than the body, creating a mask-like appearance, you've likely found a Darkface Arion rather than its plainer cousins.
contextualKnowledge: This slug goes by several common names including 'brown soil slug' and 'Mabille's orange-soled slug,' which can create confusion when consulting different field guides or websites. The name 'April slug' hints at its spring activity peak, though it's active beyond just April in New England's climate.
compareHints: Among New England's Arion slugs, the Darkface Arion is most easily distinguished by its characteristic dark facial markings, while the Garden Arion tends to be more uniformly colored and the Black Slug is typically much larger and darker overall. The Orange-banded Arion has distinctive orange or yellow bands along its sides, making it quite different in appearance from the more subtly marked Darkface Arion.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Among New England's Arion slugs, the Western Dusky Slug is one of the smallest and plainest-looking members of its genus.
Among its Arion relatives, the hedgehog slug is most distinctive for its defensive curling behavior - the Black Slug and Garden Arion don't ball up nearly as dramatically.
Garden Arions are smaller and more compact than their relatives like the Black Slug, which can grow much larger and stays more elongated when disturbed.

Black Slugs are the largest and most robust of the Arion genus in New England, with that distinctive rounded back that sets them apart from their smaller, more elongated relatives like the Western Dusky Slug or Garden Arion.
Within the Arion genus, the Northern Dusky Slug is much smaller and more subdued in color compared to the large, jet-black Black Slug or the distinctively marked Orange-banded Arion.

Among its Arion relatives in New England, the Orange-banded Arion is the only one with prominent orange side bands - the Black Slug is uniformly dark, the Garden Arion is typically smaller and grayer, and the Dusky Slugs lack any bright coloration.
